# API reference

## The C ABI

The headers of `sdk/include/shard` are the contract between a plugin and the engine. This page is them, in reading order : their comments are the documentation. See [Plugins](concepts/plugins.md#the-c-abi-and-the-sdk) for the concepts and [the tutorial](tutorials.md) to build a plugin.

Every function says the thread it may be called from : **any**, **system** (from inside a system, in parallel with others) or **main** (the main thread, outside the systems). A function returns a `ShardResult` : `SHARD_OK` (0) or a negative error, the details in the engine's log under the plugin's id. Strings are `ShardStr` (UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated, valid for the call) ; a *text out* function takes `(buffer, capacity, *size)`, copies what fits and gives the full length.

### shard_abi.h

Shard C ABI : base types, versions and rules. Compiles as C11 and as C++17.

These headers ARE the ABI (see `docs/design-notes/c-abi-sdk.fr.md`, section 3). The rules :

* plain C : no classes, references, overloads or `enum class`; no `int`, `long`, `bool` or `size_t` inside a struct
* every struct that crosses the boundary starts with `uint32_t structSize`; fields are only ever added at the END
* the host never keeps a pointer it was handed unless the doc of that function says so
* no exception crosses the boundary; failures are a `ShardResult`

Changing a struct without bumping `SHARD_ABI_MINOR` is a bug : `tests/plugins/abi_layout_tests.cpp` pins every layout.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_ABI_MAJOR` | `1` |  |
| `SHARD_ABI_MINOR` | `2` |  |

Calling convention of every function pointer in the tables. Empty on `x86_64` and arm64.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_CALL` |  |  |
| `SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT` | depends on the platform |  |

**Results**

```c
typedef int32_t ShardResult;
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_OK` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` | `(-1)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` | `(-2)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` | `(-3)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD` | `(-4)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` | `(-5)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` | `(-6)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY` | `(-7)` |  |
| `SHARD_E_INTERNAL` | `(-8)` |  |
| `SHARD_FALSE` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_TRUE` | `1` |  |

#### ShardStr

**Strings**

UTF-8, not necessarily zero terminated. A string received through a call is valid for that call only : keeping it means copying it.

```c
const char* data;
uint64_t size;
```

**Handles**

Never a pointer to a host object. index + generation, so a stale one fails instead of reading freed memory. 0 is never valid.

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardPluginCtx;    // designates a plugin to the host
typedef uint64_t ShardState;    // the reload state being written or read : valid during on_prepare_reload / on_restore only (shard_state.h)
```

**Log levels**

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_LOG_INFO` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_LOG_WARNING` | `1` |  |
| `SHARD_LOG_ERROR` | `2` |  |

### shard_host.h

Shard C ABI : what a plugin exports and what the host gives it.

#### ShardHostApi

**The host's table**

One static table for every plugin; a plugin designates itself with the `ShardPluginCtx` it is handed in each callback. The base is only what is needed to start; everything else is an interface fetched with `query_interface`, so this table barely grows.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;
ShardStr engineVersion;    // "0.9.2", informative
```

thread : any

```c
void log(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint32_t level, ShardStr message);
```

Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB). Returns NULL on failure. What is allocated here is freed with `free` here : never with the plugin's own allocator, and never by the host's.

```c
void* alloc(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t size, uint64_t align);
void free(ShardPluginCtx ctx, void* p);
```

Looks an interface up by id (`"shard.plugin"`). `major` must match; the interface must be at least `minMinor`. On success `*out` points to a struct that starts with `uint32_t structSize`, valid until the host exits. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : the id is unknown, or this host does not offer it (an offline tool has no `"shard.systems"`).

```c
ShardResult query_interface(ShardStr id, uint32_t major, uint32_t minMinor, const void** out);
```

#### ShardWorldInfo

A world a module is told about. `name` is valid for the call.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
int32_t assetId;    // the world's asset id in the project, -1 if it has none
ShardStr name;
```

#### ShardPluginCallbacks

**The plugin's callbacks**

Same order and meaning as IPlugin. A callback returns `SHARD_OK`, or an error that makes the host fail the plugin (and the plugins that depend on it) with the message the plugin logged. Every callback is optional : NULL means `"nothing to do"`. All of them run on the main thread.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
ShardResult on_load(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_initialize(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_enable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_disable(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_unload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
```

Hot reload (`shard_state.h`). `on_prepare_reload` writes what must survive into `state` and returns `SHARD_OK` ; any other result (or no callback) makes the plugin not reloadable. `on_restore` reads it back in the new binary, after `on_enable`.

```c
ShardResult on_prepare_reload(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);
ShardResult on_restore(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardState state);
```

Start and end of every frame while the plugin is enabled. Keep them short : their time is billed to the plugin.

```c
ShardResult on_frame_begin(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);
ShardResult on_frame_end(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t frame);
```

Modules : the content folder is mounted (`mod://<id>/` is readable, `shard_content.h`), and what happens to the worlds

```c
ShardResult on_content_mounted(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx);
ShardResult on_world_loaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_world_unloaded(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_start(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
ShardResult on_play_stop(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardWorldInfo* world);
```

Offline tools : the tool is about to run `task` (`"cook"`, `"bake"`, `"validate"`) on the project file `project`. `SHARD_OK` lets it run ; anything else cancels it, with `*message` (copied before the call returns) as the reason. Unlike the others, an error here does not fail the plugin.

```c
ShardResult on_tool_task(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr task, ShardStr project, ShardStr* message);
```

Callbacks of later ABI revisions go HERE : the host checks structSize before reading them.

#### ShardPluginInfo

What the plugin fills in its entry point

```c
uint32_t structSize;    // the plugin sets it to sizeof(ShardPluginInfo) of the headers it was built with ; the host reads no field past it
uint32_t abiMajor, abiMinor;    // the plugin sets them to SHARD_ABI_MAJOR / SHARD_ABI_MINOR
ShardStr id;    // informative : the manifest is what the host trusts
void* user;    // handed back to every callback
const ShardPluginCallbacks* callbacks;    // must stay valid until on_unload returned
```

The entry point of an ABI `"c1"` plugin (manifest `"abi"`: `"c1"`). Called once, right after the library is loaded, on the main thread. `out` is zeroed. Return `SHARD_OK`, or an error to refuse to load.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardPluginEntryFn)(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_PLUGIN_ENTRY_NAME` | `"shard_plugin_entry"` |  |

```c
SHARD_PLUGIN_EXPORT ShardResult shard_plugin_entry(const ShardHostApi* host, ShardPluginInfo* out);
```

### shard_cvars.h

Interface `"shard.cvars"` 1.0 : variables the plugin owns, readable from the console and the config files like the engine's own. A variable is named `"<plugin id>.<name>"` by the host. It lives until the plugin is disabled or unloaded ; after that its handle is stale (`SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE`). The plugin changes its own variables with `set_*` (that bypasses the config layers and the read-only flag, as the owner) ; the console and the config files change them from outside. Numeric values are clamped to [min, max].

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_CVARS` | `"shard.cvars"` |  |
| `SHARD_CVAR_READONLY` | `1u` | the console and the config files cannot change it |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardCVar;    // generation << 32 | slot ; 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardCVarsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

thread : main. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if the name is taken.

```c
ShardResult create_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, int32_t min, int32_t max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, float value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, float min, float max, ShardCVar* out);
ShardResult create_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr value, ShardStr help, uint32_t flags, ShardCVar* out);
```

thread : any. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` if the variable is of another type.

```c
ShardResult get_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t* out);
ShardResult get_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float* out);
```

Copies at most `capacity` bytes (no zero terminator) into `buffer` and stores the full length in `*size` : a value longer than the buffer is cut, and the caller can call again with a bigger one. `buffer` may be NULL to ask for the length.

```c
ShardResult get_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);
```

thread : main

```c
ShardResult set_bool(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_int(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, int32_t value);
ShardResult set_float(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, float value);
ShardResult set_string(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardCVar cvar, ShardStr value);
```

### shard_commands.h

Interface `"shard.commands"` 1.0 : console commands. The command is removed with the plugin (disable or unload).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_COMMANDS` | `"shard.commands"` |  |

Runs the command. `args` are the words after the command name (`argCount` of them, valid for the call). The callback may point `*output` to a text to show the user (it is copied before the callback's caller returns : a static buffer or the plugin's own will do). Return `SHARD_OK` for success ; anything else is shown as a failure, with the output as the message. thread : main

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardCommandFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardStr* args, uint32_t argCount, ShardStr* output);
```

#### ShardCommandsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

The name is used as given : prefix it with your own (`"weather.set"`). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if this plugin already added that name (case does not matter). A name another plugin or the engine already uses is replaced for as long as this plugin lives : the prefix is what keeps commands apart. thread : main

```c
ShardResult add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr help, ShardCommandFn run, void* user);
```

### shard_components.h

Interface `"shard.components"` 1.1 : component types described field by field.

One registration gives a type two faces, under one name (`"<plugin id>.<name>"`, made by the host) :

* an ECS component : a block of `size` bytes on an entity, what systems query and write (`shard_ecs.h`). Plain data : copied with memcpy,
```
never constructed nor destroyed, so no pointer to memory the plugin owns. What does not fit in the block goes in a blob (1.1, below) ;
```

* an actor component : what a world file saves, the editor shows in its inspector and an actor carries. Its fields are the ones described
```
here, read and written at their offset in the block.
```

An actor that has the actor component has the ECS component on its entity, with the same values : the actor component writes its values to the entity when it is loaded, edited or attached, and reads them back from the entity when the world is saved or copied. So what a system changed is what gets saved. An entity a plugin spawned on its own (`shard_ecs.h`, `cmd_spawn`) has no actor : it is not saved.

The type lives as long as the plugin is enabled. Its ECS id stays reserved for the whole run : a plugin enabled again gets the same `ShardComponentType` back, provided it describes the same size (a type whose size changed needs a restart of the engine).

Blobs (1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside the block, as many as needed (a chunk of voxels), counted against the plugin's memory budget. A field `SHARD_FIELD_BLOB` holds the `ShardBlob` handle. The plugin owns its blobs : `blob_free` gives one back, and all of them go with the plugin (disable, unload). The block is still copied with memcpy, so two blocks may hold the same handle : that is a shared blob, not a copy. The actor component is the exception, it owns the blobs of its blob fields : it saves their bytes with the world (base64), a copy of the actor (play mode) gets copies of them, and removing the component frees them. A system that puts a new blob in such a field frees the one it replaces.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_COMPONENTS` | `"shard.components"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardComponentType;    // 0 is never valid
typedef uint64_t ShardBlob;    // 0 is never valid : an empty blob field
```

Field types : the C type the field has in the block, and how it is saved

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_FIELD_F32` | `1u` | float |
| `SHARD_FIELD_F64` | `2u` | double |
| `SHARD_FIELD_I32` | `3u` | `int32_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_U32` | `4u` | `uint32_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_I64` | `5u` | `int64_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_U64` | `6u` | `uint64_t` |
| `SHARD_FIELD_BOOL` | `7u` | `uint8_t`, 0 or 1 |
| `SHARD_FIELD_VEC2` | `8u` | float[2] |
| `SHARD_FIELD_VEC3` | `9u` | float[3] |
| `SHARD_FIELD_VEC4` | `10u` | float[4] |
| `SHARD_FIELD_QUAT` | `11u` | float[4] : x, y, z, w |
| `SHARD_FIELD_COLOR` | `12u` | float[4] : r, g, b, a (the inspector shows a colour picker) |
| `SHARD_FIELD_BLOB` | `13u` | `ShardBlob` (`uint64_t`) : saved as the blob's bytes, not shown by the inspector (1.1) |

Field flags. Without any, a field is saved and editable in the inspector.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME` | `1u` | runtime state : shown by the inspector, read only, not saved |
| `SHARD_FIELD_PRIVATE` | `2u` | neither shown nor saved : the block keeps it, nothing else sees it |

#### ShardFieldDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t type;    // SHARD_FIELD_*
ShardStr name;    // letters, digits and '_' ; "type", "active" and "tags" are reserved
uint32_t offset;    // in the block, aligned for its type
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_FIELD_RUNTIME...
float min, max;    // bounds of the inspector's widget ; min == max : none
ShardStr tooltip;    // optional
```

#### ShardComponentDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t size;    // bytes of the block, 1 to SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_SIZE
uint32_t align;    // a power of two, 16 at most
uint32_t fieldCount;    // SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_FIELDS at most
ShardStr name;    // "Spin" : the host registers "<plugin id>.Spin"
const ShardFieldDesc* fields;    // read during the call only
const void* defaults;    // `size` bytes : the value of a new component. NULL : zeroes. Read during the call only.
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_SIZE` | `1024u` |  |
| `SHARD_COMPONENT_MAX_FIELDS` | `64u` |  |

#### ShardComponentsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Registers a type, from `on_load`. thread : main. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : a field out of the block, misaligned, overlapping another, of an unknown type, a bad name, a size or an alignment out of bounds (the log says which). `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : the name is taken (by this plugin, or by a type of another size).

```c
ShardResult register_type(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardComponentDesc* desc, ShardComponentType* out);
```

The type of that full name (`"com.acme.weather.Cloud"`) : one of a C plugin, or one of the engine's that `shard_ecs.h` documents (`"shard.LocalTransform"`...). thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` if there is none.

```c
ShardResult find_type(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardComponentType* out);
```

Size and alignment of the block. thread : any

```c
ShardResult type_layout(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t* size, uint32_t* align);
```

The fields of a type a C plugin registered (another plugin's, to read its blocks without its header). `out->structSize` must be set by the caller ; the strings in `*out` stay valid while that type is registered. thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such field / index.

```c
ShardResult field_count(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t* count);
ShardResult field_at(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, uint32_t index, ShardFieldDesc* out);
ShardResult find_field(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardComponentType type, ShardStr name, ShardFieldDesc* out);
```

**1.1 : blobs**

A blob of `size` bytes, zeroed (size may be 0). thread : any. `SHARD_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY` : over the plugin's enforced budget.

```c
ShardResult blob_create(ShardPluginCtx ctx, uint64_t size, ShardBlob* out);
```

Its bytes and size. The pointer stays valid until the blob is resized or freed ; reading and writing them from several threads at once is the plugin's to order (a system that writes a blob declares the component that holds it in its writes). thread : any. `SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE` : freed, or not this plugin's.

```c
ShardResult blob_data(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob, void** data, uint64_t* size);
```

New size, the first bytes kept, the rest zeroed ; the bytes move. thread : any

```c
ShardResult blob_resize(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob, uint64_t size);
ShardResult blob_free(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardBlob blob);
```

### shard_ecs.h

Interface `"shard.ecs"` 1.0 : entities and their components, from inside a system (`shard_systems.h`).

Every function takes the `ShardEcs` the system was handed in its `ShardSystemCtx` : it is valid during that run, on that thread, and nowhere else (`SHARD_E_STALE_HANDLE`). A system reads and writes only the types it declared (reads / writes of its `ShardSystemDesc`, `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` otherwise ; an exclusive system may touch anything) : the scheduler relies on these declarations to run systems in parallel, and the result of a frame must not depend on it.

Structural changes (spawn, destroy, add, remove, `set_parent`) are recorded and applied at the end of the phase, system by system in registration order. spawn returns a placeholder that the later commands of the same run can use ; it means nothing afterwards. Changing the VALUE of a component (through the pointers of `each_chunk` and get) is immediate.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_ECS` | `"shard.ecs"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardEntity;    // generation << 32 | index ; 0 is the null entity
typedef uint64_t ShardEcs;    // the registry as one system run sees it
```

#### ShardQuery

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t withCount;
uint32_t withoutCount;
const ShardComponentType* with;    // the entities have all of these ; the chunk's columns come in this order
const ShardComponentType* without;    // and none of these
```

#### ShardChunk

`count` entities that have the same components. columns[i] holds `count` blocks of query.with[i], one after the other : block j is at (char\*)columns[i] + j \* size of that type. Valid during the callback only.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t count;
const ShardEntity* entities;
void* const* columns;
```

Return `SHARD_OK` to go on ; anything else stops the iteration and is what `each_chunk` returns.

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardChunkFn)(void* user, const ShardChunk* chunk);
```

#### ShardEcsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Calls fn once per chunk of matching entities, in a stable order. No structural change happens meanwhile. thread : system

```c
ShardResult each_chunk(ShardEcs ecs, const ShardQuery* query, ShardChunkFn fn, void* user);
```

How many entities match. thread : system

```c
ShardResult count(ShardEcs ecs, const ShardQuery* query, uint64_t* out);
```

`SHARD_TRUE` if the entity exists (a placeholder of spawn does not, yet). thread : system

```c
int32_t is_alive(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity);
```

The entity's block of `type`, valid until the end of the run. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : it has none (or is dead). thread : system

```c
ShardResult get(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type, void** out);
```

The parent (the null entity for a root). thread : system

```c
ShardResult parent(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardEntity* out);
```

Recorded, applied at the end of the phase. thread : system

```c
ShardResult spawn(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity* placeholder);
ShardResult destroy(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity);    // and its descendants
```

Adds the component, or overwrites its value. `size` must be the size of the type ; `data` is copied now.

```c
ShardResult add(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type, const void* data, uint64_t size);
ShardResult remove(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity entity, ShardComponentType type);
ShardResult set_parent(ShardEcs ecs, ShardEntity child, ShardEntity parent);    // null parent : detach
```

**The engine's own components, found by name with `shard.components`' `find_type`**

Read them ; do not write them : the actor's components are what drives them, and they overwrite what a system writes.

#### ShardLocalTransform

`"shard.LocalTransform"` : on the entity of every actor, its Transform relative to its parent

```c
float position[3];
float rotation[4];    // quaternion x, y, z, w
float scale[3];
```

#### ShardActorLink

`"shard.ActorLink"` : on the entity of every actor, the actor's object id

```c
int32_t objectId;
```

`"shard.Disabled"` (1 byte, no field) : on the entity of an actor that is deactivated. Put it in `without` to skip those.

### shard_systems.h

Interface `"shard.systems"` 1.0 : functions the engine's scheduler runs every frame, in a phase, in parallel with the systems they do not conflict with (one writes what the other reads or writes). A system is named `"<plugin id>/<name>"` by the host and is removed with the plugin. A system added before the engine built its scheduler (from `on_load`) starts with the first frame.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SYSTEMS` | `"shard.systems"` |  |

The phases of a frame, always run in this order. Fixed runs 0..N times per frame (as many fixed steps as the elapsed time pays for).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_PHASE_INPUT` | `0u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_PRE_SIM` | `1u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_FIXED` | `2u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_POST_PHYSICS` | `3u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_UPDATE` | `4u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_LATE` | `5u` |  |
| `SHARD_PHASE_EXTRACT` | `6u` |  |
| `SHARD_SYSTEM_EXCLUSIVE` | `1u` | touches what reads / writes cannot say : runs alone, in order |
| `SHARD_SYSTEM_MAIN_THREAD` | `2u` | needs the thread that runs the frame : the phase then runs on it, in order |

#### ShardSystemCtx

What a run of a system is given. Valid during the run only.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
float deltaTime;    // the variable step ; the fixed step in SHARD_PHASE_FIXED
float fixedDeltaTime;
int32_t fixedStep;    // SHARD_PHASE_FIXED : index of this step in the frame, from 0
int32_t fixedStepCount;    // SHARD_PHASE_FIXED : how many steps this frame runs
uint64_t frame;
ShardEcs ecs;    // for shard.ecs
```

Returns `SHARD_OK`. Any other result is counted as an error of the plugin ; at the tenth, the host fails it. thread : the system's

```c
typedef ShardResult (*ShardSystemFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardSystemCtx* run);
```

#### ShardSystemDesc

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t phase;    // SHARD_PHASE_*
uint32_t flags;    // SHARD_SYSTEM_*
uint32_t readCount, writeCount;
uint32_t afterCount, beforeCount;
ShardStr name;    // "rotate" : registered as "<plugin id>/rotate"
const ShardComponentType* reads;
const ShardComponentType* writes;
```

Explicit order, systems of the same phase only. A full name (`"com.acme.weather/wind"`), or `"./x"` for this plugin's `"x"`.

```c
const ShardStr* after;
const ShardStr* before;
ShardSystemFn run;
void* user;    // handed back to run
```

#### ShardSystemsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Everything in desc is copied. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : this plugin has a system of that name. thread : main

```c
ShardResult add(ShardPluginCtx ctx, const ShardSystemDesc* desc);
```

`name` as given to add. thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such system of this plugin.

```c
ShardResult set_enabled(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t enabled);
ShardResult remove(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name);
```

### shard_events.h

Interface `"shard.events"` 1.1 : events found by NAME, carrying bytes.

The engine's C++ events are found by their C++ type, which a binary built by another compiler cannot name : the C ABI has a channel of its own, where an event is a name (`"com.acme.weather.RainStarted"`) and a payload of bytes whose layout the sender documents. C++ code reaches the same channel (`EventRegistrar::SubscribeNamed` / EmitNamed). Subscriptions end with the plugin (disable or unload).

Delivery : an event emitted on the main thread outside of the systems is delivered at once, to the subscribers in the order they subscribed. One emitted from a system (any thread) is queued and delivered on the main thread at the end of the frame, the queues of the systems taken in the order of their names : the order does not depend on which system finished first.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EVENTS` | `"shard.events"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardSubscription;    // 0 is never valid
```

`name` and `payload` are valid for the call. thread : main

```c
typedef void (*ShardEventFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
```

#### ShardEventsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Events sent globally under `name`. thread : main

```c
ShardResult subscribe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardEventFn fn, void* user, ShardSubscription* out);
```

Events sent to one world (its asset id) under `name`. thread : main

```c
ShardResult subscribe_world(ShardPluginCtx ctx, int32_t worldId, ShardStr name, ShardEventFn fn, void* user, ShardSubscription* out);
```

thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : not one of this plugin's live subscriptions.

```c
ShardResult unsubscribe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardSubscription subscription);
```

The payload is copied. thread : any (see the delivery rules above). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the engine has no dispatcher (an offline tool).

```c
ShardResult emit(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
ShardResult emit_world(ShardPluginCtx ctx, int32_t worldId, ShardStr name, const void* payload, uint64_t size);
```

**1.1**

Says what the payload of the events named `name` holds, field by field (the fields of `shard_components.h`, offsets in the payload), so that the tools can show them : the console's event.watch prints each one. One description per name : `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` if another plugin described it. It goes with the plugin. Optional : events nobody described are shown as their size. thread : main

```c
ShardResult describe(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, uint32_t size, const ShardFieldDesc* fields, uint32_t fieldCount);
```

### shard_hooks.h

Interface `"shard.hooks"` 1.0 : the points of the engine a plugin can intercept, and cancel. Hooks are found by name ; every one is described by the same struct, whose `subject`, `detail` and `frame` mean what the table below says. Handlers run by priority, then by plugin load order, then in the order they were added : the same order on every run. They are removed with the plugin.

```
name                 subject             detail          frame
"PreEngineInit"      -                   -               -
"PostEngineInit"     -                   -               -
"PreWorldLoad"       the world's name    -               -       cancellable : the world is not loaded
"PostWorldLoad"      the world's name    -               -
"PrePlay"            -                   -               -       cancellable : play mode does not start
"PostPlay"           -                   -               -
"PreFrame"           -                   -               frame
"PostFrame"          -                   -               frame
"PreSave"            what is saved       -               -       cancellable : nothing is saved
"AssetImported"      the asset's path    -               -
"PlayerConnecting"   the client's name   its address     -       cancellable : the client is refused, `reason` is what it is told
"PreShutdown"        -                   -               -
```

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_HOOKS` | `"shard.hooks"` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_EARLIEST` | `(-200)` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_EARLY` | `(-100)` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_NORMAL` | `0` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_LATE` | `100` |  |
| `SHARD_PRIORITY_LATEST` | `200` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardHookToken;    // 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardHookArgs

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint8_t cancelled;    // in : an earlier handler cancelled ; out : set it to 1 to cancel (a later handler may see it and set it back)
uint8_t reserved[3];
ShardStr name;    // the hook's name
ShardStr subject;    // see the table ; valid for the call
ShardStr detail;
uint64_t frame;
ShardStr reason;    // out : why it was cancelled, copied when the handler returns
```

thread : main

```c
typedef void (*ShardHookFn)(void* user, ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardHookArgs* hook);
```

#### ShardHooksApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

`name` from the table above (`SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` otherwise). thread : main

```c
ShardResult on(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, int32_t priority, ShardHookFn fn, void* user, ShardHookToken* out);
ShardResult off(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardHookToken token);
```

### shard_services.h

Interface `"shard.services"` 1.0 : interfaces plugins offer each other, by name and version, without including each other's code.

A service of the C ABI is a table of function pointers that starts with `uint32_t structSize` (and, like the ABI's own tables, only grows at its end), plus a `self` the functions get back. The provider publishes the header of its table ; the users include it. The engine never calls the table : it only hands it out.

A user holds a `ShardServiceRef`, not the table : resolve it before each use. When the provider is disabled or unloaded, the ref resolves to nothing (`SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND`) instead of to a table in a library that is gone. Refs are released with the plugin that took them.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_SERVICES` | `"shard.services"` |  |

```c
typedef uint64_t ShardServiceRef;    // 0 is never valid
```

#### ShardService

```c
uint32_t structSize;
uint32_t major, minor;    // the version the provider offers
const void* table;    // the provider's table (its first field is its structSize)
void* self;
```

#### ShardServicesApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

Offers `table` and `self` as service `name` (copied ; `table` must stay valid until the plugin is disabled). thread : main. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : another plugin provides that name.

```c
ShardResult provide(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, uint32_t major, uint32_t minor, const void* table, void* self);
```

A ref on the service `name` if its version is in `range` (`"^1.2"`, `">=1"`, `"*"`). thread : main. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : nobody provides it, or not in that range ; `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : the range does not parse.

```c
ShardResult get(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr name, ShardStr range, ShardServiceRef* out);
```

What the ref points to now (the caller sets out-&gt;structSize ; the host fills what fits). thread : any. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : its provider went away ; `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the provider is not a plugin of the C ABI (its object is not a `ShardService`).

```c
ShardResult resolve(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardServiceRef ref, ShardService* out);
ShardResult release(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardServiceRef ref);
```

### shard_extensions.h

Interface `"shard.extensions"` 1.0 : what a plugin adds to the engine's subsystems through their extension points. The C ABI offers the points whose items are only data and functions :

```
"tool.validator"   a check the asset validator (ShardAssetValidator) runs on a project
"asset.type"       a kind of asset : file extensions the project indexes, and the loader the resource cache calls
"asset.importer"   a converter from a source format the engine does not read to files it does
```

Every item is copied by the host (strings and arrays included), named, and removed with the plugin. The functions run on the main thread.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EXTENSIONS` | `"shard.extensions"` |  |
| `SHARD_POINT_TOOL_VALIDATOR` | `"tool.validator"` |  |
| `SHARD_POINT_ASSET_TYPE` | `"asset.type"` |  |
| `SHARD_POINT_ASSET_IMPORTER` | `"asset.importer"` |  |

#### ShardReport

Where a validator or an importer writes what it found or made. `host` is handed back as is. Valid during the call only.

```c
uint32_t structSize;
void* host;
```

A validator : one problem per call. An importer : a file it wrote (absolute path).

```c
void add(void* host, ShardStr line);
```

An importer : why it failed, or a note on what it did.

```c

```

#### ShardValidatorItem



thread : main. `SHARD_E_ALREADY_EXISTS` : the point has an item of that name.

### shard_content.h

Interface `"shard.content"` 1.0 : the content folders of the loaded modules. Every module with content is mounted as `mod://<id>/` ; the same files form one layered tree by logical path (`"materials/stone.mat"`), later modules winning where they say they override (see the docs, `"Content"`). Nothing here leaves the mounted folders. thread : any (the mounts change only while plugins load and unload, on the main thread).

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_CONTENT` | `"shard.content"` |  |

Called once per file, with its path relative to the folder listed ('/' separators). Return `SHARD_OK` to go on.

The `mod://` address of a file of this plugin (`"textures/a.png"` -&gt; `"mod://<id>/textures/a.png"`). Text out : copies at most `capacity` bytes (no zero terminator) and stores the full length in `*size` ; `buffer` may be NULL to ask for the length.

```c
ShardResult uri_of(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardStr path, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);
```

### shard_state.h

Interface `"shard.state"` 1.0 : what a plugin keeps across a hot reload. `on_prepare_reload` (`shard_host.h`) writes values into the `ShardState` it is handed, the new binary reads them back in `on_restore`. Values are JSON text (an object, a number, a string in quotes...) : the format does not depend on the memory layout, so the new binary may have changed its structs. The handle is valid during that callback only. thread : main

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_STATE` | `"shard.state"` |  |

#### ShardStateApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

`on_prepare_reload`. `SHARD_E_INVALID_ARG` : `json` does not parse.

```c

```

`on_restore`. The value of `key` as JSON text (compact) ; copies at most `capacity` bytes (no zero terminator) and stores the full length in `*size` ; `buffer` may be NULL to ask for the length. `SHARD_E_NOT_FOUND` : no such key.

```c
ShardResult get(ShardState state, ShardStr key, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity, uint64_t* size);

```

### shard_experimental.h

Interface `"shard.experimental.world_ecs"` 0.1 : the engine's entities from the main thread, outside the systems.

The interfaces named `"shard.experimental.*"` are offered so that what may still change can be tried before it is frozen into the ABI. They carry NO compatibility promise : one may change or disappear in any revision of the engine. Their major is 0, and `query_interface` hands one out only for the exact minor the engine has (`query_interface`(`"shard.experimental.world_ecs"`, 0, 1, ...)) : a plugin built against another one does not get it. A native plugin that carries a valid signature of a trusted publisher (what is distributed) is refused them : every function returns `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED`. Their structs are not pinned by the layout tests.

`world_ecs` : `open()` gives a `ShardEcs` over the engine's registry that every function of `shard.ecs` (`shard_ecs.h`) accepts, as an exclusive system would (any type) ; the structural changes are applied by `close()`. Between the two, the main thread functions of the other interfaces keep working. Open and close in the same callback ; what a plugin leaves open is closed when its context goes.

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARD_IFACE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORLD_ECS` | `"shard.experimental.world_ecs"` |  |

#### ShardWorldEcsApi

```c
uint32_t structSize;
```

thread : main, outside the systems and while no phase runs (`SHARD_E_WRONG_THREAD`). `SHARD_E_UNSUPPORTED` : the plugin may not use experimental interfaces, or this host has no registry (an offline tool).

```c
ShardResult open(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardEcs* out);
```

Applies the structural changes recorded since open, in order. The last opened first.

```c
ShardResult close(ShardPluginCtx ctx, ShardEcs ecs);
```

## The C++ SDK

`sdk/include/shard/cpp` : header-only C++17 over the C ABI, compiled into the plugin. `#include <shard/cpp/plugin.hpp>` brings all of it. Every callback of the SDK catches what the plugin throws : `shard::Error` (what a registration the host refused throws, with its `ShardResult`) and anything else become an error of that callback, with the message in the log. Below, the public declarations of each header (bodies left out).

### shard/cpp/plugin.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : a plugin class over the C ABI.

```cpp
class SpinPlugin : public shard::Plugin {
public:
    void OnLoad(shard::Context& ctx) override { ... }
};
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(SpinPlugin)
```

The macro exports `shard_plugin_entry` and fills the callbacks table : every callback catches what the plugin throws (`shard::Error` from a refused registration, or anything else) and turns it into an error the host fails the plugin with, the message in its log. Nothing of the engine is included or linked : this compiles against `sdk/include` alone, with any C++17 compiler.

#### `Context`

What the host knows of the plugin, and every way the plugin reaches it

```cpp
ShardPluginCtx Handle() const;
std::string_view Id() const;
std::string_view Version() const;
/// The plugin's folder, absolute
std::string_view Directory() const;
/// "editor", "player", "headless" or "tool" (empty in an engine of ABI 1.0)
std::string_view HostName() const;
/// True if the manifest asks for that permission (false in an engine of ABI 1.0)
bool HasPermission(std::string_view permission) const;
void Log(std::string_view message) const;
void Warn(std::string_view message) const;
void Error(std::string_view message) const;
/// Memory counted against the plugin's budget (manifest budgets.memoryMB) : give it back with Free
void* Alloc(size_t size, size_t align = 16) const;
void Free(void* p) const;
shard::Components Components() const;
shard::Systems Systems() const;
shard::CVars CVars() const;
shard::Commands Commands() const;
shard::Events Events() const;
shard::Hooks Hooks() const;
shard::Services Services() const;
shard::Content Content() const;
shard::Extensions Extensions() const;
```

#### `World`

A world a module is told about

```cpp
int32_t assetId = -1;
std::string_view name;
```

#### `Plugin`

The base of a plugin written with the SDK : the same calls, in the same order, as the engine's IPlugin (see `shard_host.h`)

```cpp
/// Register everything here (components, systems, cvars, commands, services, hooks...)
virtual void OnLoad(Context&);
/// Every plugin ran OnLoad : the services of the others can be asked for
virtual void OnInitialize(Context&);
virtual void OnEnable(Context&);
virtual void OnDisable(Context&);
virtual void OnUnload(Context&);
/// Hot reload : write what must survive and return true ; false (the default) makes the plugin not reloadable
virtual bool OnPrepareReload(Context&, StateWriter&);
virtual void OnRestore(Context&, StateReader&);
virtual void OnFrameBegin(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnFrameEnd(Context&, uint64_t /*frame*/);
virtual void OnContentMounted(Context&);
virtual void OnWorldLoaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnWorldUnloaded(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStart(Context&, const World&);
virtual void OnPlayStop(Context&, const World&);
/// An offline tool is about to run `task` ("cook", "bake", "validate") : return false (and a message) to cancel it
virtual bool OnToolTask(Context&, std::string_view /*task*/, std::string_view /*project*/, std::string& /*message*/);
```

```cpp
/// Exports the entry point of the C ABI for a class derived from shard::Plugin (once per plugin, in one source file)
SHARD_C_PLUGIN(ClassName)
```

### shard/cpp/component.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : component types from C++ structs.

```cpp
struct Spin { float speed = 1.f; float angle = 0.f; shard::Vec3 axis{ 0.f, 1.f, 0.f }; };
SHARD_COMPONENT(Spin, (speed)(angle)(axis))
```

(at global scope) declares which members are fields (their type and offset are deduced) ; the struct's default member values are the defaults of a new component. The struct must be trivially copyable and standard layout : it is the block the engine copies with memcpy (`shard_components.h`). Register it in OnLoad with `ctx.Components().Register<Spin>("Spin")`.

#### `Vec2`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec3`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f;
```

#### `Vec4`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 0.f;
```

#### `Quat`

```cpp
float x = 0.f, y = 0.f, z = 0.f, w = 1.f;
```

#### `Color`

```cpp
float r = 1.f, g = 1.f, b = 1.f, a = 1.f;
```

#### `FieldType<float>, FieldType<double>, FieldType<int32_t>, FieldType<uint32_t>, FieldType<int64_t>, FieldType<uint64_t>, FieldType<bool>, FieldType<Vec2>, FieldType<Vec3>, FieldType<Vec4>, FieldType<Quat>, FieldType<Color>, FieldType<float[2]>, FieldType<float[3]>, FieldType<float[4]>, FieldType<Blob>`

The `SHARD_FIELD_*` of a member type. Specialize it for a type of your own with the same layout (`glm::vec3` -&gt; `SHARD_FIELD_VEC3`).

```cpp
static constexpr uint32_t value = 0;
```

#### `Blob`

A blob of this plugin (`shard_components.h`, 1.1) : bytes the host keeps outside a component's block, as many as needed. A component holds one in a member of this type ; `Components::CreateBlob` makes it. Copying the struct copies the handle, not the bytes.

```cpp
ShardBlob handle = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `FieldOptions`

### shard/cpp/system.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : systems and what they see of the entities.

```cpp
ctx.Systems().Add("rotate", shard::Phase::Update)
    .Writes(spin)
    .Run([spin](shard::SystemCtx& s) {
        s.Each(spin, [&](Spin& c) { c.angle += c.speed * s.DeltaTime(); });
    });
```

A system reads and writes only the types it declared (Reads / Writes) : the scheduler runs systems in parallel on that promise.

```cpp
using Entity = ShardEntity;
enum class Phase : uint32_t { Input = SHARD_PHASE_INPUT, PreSim = SHARD_PHASE_PRE_SIM, Fixed = SHARD_PHASE_FIXED, PostPhysics = SHARD_PHASE_POST_PHYSICS, Update = SHARD_PHASE_UPDATE, Late = SHARD_PHASE_LATE, Extract = SHARD_PHASE_EXTRACT, };
```

#### `EntityQuery`

The entities that have all of Cs (and none of the Without types), seen from one run of a system

```cpp

/// fn(Cs&...) or fn(Entity, Cs&...), once per entity
template <typename F> void Each(F&& fn);
/// fn(count, const Entity* entities, Cs*... columns) : the tightest loop, once per chunk
template <typename F> void EachChunk(F&& fn);
uint64_t Count() const;
```

```cpp
template <typename C, typename F> void Each(ComponentType<C> type, F&& fn) const;
template <typename A, typename B, typename F> void Each(ComponentType<A> a, ComponentType<B> b, F&& fn) const;
bool IsAlive(Entity e) const;
/// The entity's component, null if it has none. Valid until the end of the run.
```

#### `World`

The engine's registry from the main thread, outside the systems : `shard.experimental.world_ecs` 0.1, with NO compatibility promise (`shard_experimental.h`). Every function of the SystemCtx it gives works, on any type ; the structural changes are applied when it goes. Refused to a native plugin signed by a trusted publisher. Use it inside one callback.

```cpp
World& operator=(const World&) = delete;
SystemCtx& Ecs();
```

### shard/cpp/services.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : services between plugins (`shard_services.h`). A service is a C table of function pointers that starts with `uint32_t structSize`, published in a header by its provider :

```cpp
struct WeatherApi { uint32_t structSize; float (SHARD_CALL *rain)(void* self, float x, float z); };
ctx.Services().Provide("weather.query", 1, 0, &kWeatherApi, this);                 // the provider
auto weather = ctx.Services().Get<WeatherApi>("weather.query", "^1");              // a user, in OnInitialize
if (auto w = weather.Resolve()) w.table->rain(w.self, 0.f, 0.f);                   // before each use
```

#### `Resolved`

A service resolved now : its table and the provider's `self`. Do not keep it : resolve again before each use.

```cpp
const Table* table = nullptr;
void* self = nullptr;
uint32_t major = 0, minor = 0;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `Service`

A handle on a service : empty once its provider is disabled or unloaded

```cpp
Resolved<Table> Resolve() const;
explicit operator bool() const;
```

#### `Services`

```cpp
/// `table` stays valid until the plugin is disabled (a static table). Throws shard::Error if another plugin provides the name.
template <typename Table> void Provide(const std::string& name, uint32_t major, uint32_t minor, const Table* table, void* self) const;
/// Empty if nobody provides it in that range ("^1.2", ">=1", "*")
template <typename Table> Service<Table> Get(const std::string& name, const std::string& range = "*") const;
```

### shard/cpp/string.hpp

Shard C++ SDK : strings across the C ABI. Header-only, C++17 : compiled into the plugin, so it may use the standard library freely without touching the ABI (`sdk/include/shard/*.h` is the ABI ; nothing here crosses it but C types).

```cpp
/// A view as the ABI's string. The view must outlive the call it is passed to.
inline ShardStr Str(std::string_view s);
inline ShardStr Str(const char* s);
inline ShardStr Str(const std::string& s);
/// The ABI's string as a view : valid as long as the call that handed it
inline std::string_view View(ShardStr s);
inline std::string ToString(ShardStr s);
/// Reads a "text out" function of the ABI (buffer, capacity, *size) into a std::string : asks for the length, then the text.
template <typename Fn> ShardResult ReadText(Fn&& call, std::string& out);
```
